newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia, U.S. mull joint anti-competition attack.
newsitem.headline: Australia, U.S. mull joint anti-competition attack.

text.p: Australia and the United States are considering a pact to share information and evidence to help authorities combat breaches of competition law, the Australia Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) said on Friday.
ACCC chairman Allan Fels said in a statement the global economy meant increasing involvement of authorities in different countries to enforce competition laws.
Fels said Prime Minister John Howard was seeking state and territory comment on a draft treaty with the U.S.
"Accordingly, it is essential competition law agencies develop means of assisting each other to investigate contraventions that extend to other countries," Fels said in a statement.
"The initiative clearly demonstrates that Australia is committed to two-way co-operation on the enforcement of competition laws."
Under the planned agreement, Australia and the United States would exchange evidence and help each other gather evidence.
